title: Enhancing Digital Microfluidic Biochip Operations with Scheduling Interval Method
problem: Digital Microfluidic Biochip (DMFB) sample preparation involves complex mixing sequences with constraints on fluid usage, mixer availability, storage capacity, and chemical waste. Existing scheduling algorithms do not jointly optimize all these parameters.
motivation: Lab-on-Chip devices require efficient sample preparation minimizing resource usage, chemical waste, and completion time. Better scheduling algorithms can improve resource utilization and enable more complex assays on limited chip hardware.
method: Interval-based scheduling algorithm for DMFB sample preparation that minimizes: (1) input pipes, (2) mixer units, (3) storage units, (4) mixing counts, (5) storage counts, (6) fluid shifting operations. Evaluated against Reservoir Minimizing Scheduling (RMS) baseline.
key_novelty: Interval-based scheduling method achieving joint optimization of resource usage, mixing operations, and fluid shifting for DMFB sample preparation.
contributions: 21% average reduction in mixing count vs. RMS after scheduling
10% reduction in average fluid shifting vs. RMS
Minimizes input pipes, mixer units, storage units simultaneously
Reduces mixing and storage counts for improved resource efficiency
Practical algorithm for complex biochemical assay preparation
limitations: Limited to single baseline (RMS); comparison with other state-of-the-art scheduling methods absent
Evaluation metrics incomplete; no mention of algorithm runtime, scalability to large assays, or optimality gap
Specific assay test cases not detailed; generalization to diverse biochemical protocols unclear
No hardware implementation or silicon results; algorithm only
Assumes fixed chip architecture; adaptability to different biochip designs not addressed
Does not consider actuation timing or electrode conflicts that affect practical realizability
